transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (CTO - Nimbus), Meera Patel (Lead Infra), Liam O'Connor (Product), Sana Ahmed (Security)

Summary:
Quick integration/discovery focused on how Nimbus would integrate Redwood (hosted vs dedicated vs private), SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy requirements, rate limits/quotas, and observability hooks. Action items and next steps captured at end.

Topics:
- Current stack & constraints
- Integration patterns (SDK, direct REST, LangChain, LlamaIndex)
- Gateway/proxy & rate-limiting patterns
- Observability hooks (tracing, logs, token-level cost)
- Security/compliance (KMS, SOC2, VPC/private deployment)

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining. uh i'm Jordan from Redwood AE, joining me is Priya and Avery on the engineering side. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:06] Carlos: Good thanks. we got a few folks on from Nimbus. Meera, Liam, Sana on the line. thanks for doing this.
[00:00:12] Priya: great, quick agenda, want to understand your integration goals, current stack, and the non-negotiables for security and latency, then we can talk patterns for SDKs, langchain connectors, and our dedicated/private options.
[00:00:22] Liam: Sounds good. high level - product wants to ship a semantic search and PCI-sensitive docs redaction flow. latency should be 200-300ms p50 for small prompts. QPS initially low but spikey during batch payouts.
[00:00:34] Meera: For infra, we run on AWS primarily, using our own API gateway and an internal proxy layer. We use SSO (SAML) and have strict VPC restrictions for PCI scope.
[00:00:44] Sana: Security - SOC2 in progress, need KMS/HSM for key management, audit logs, and proof that data isn't persisted on shared hosts.
[00:00:52] Jordan: Great context. sounds like there are three areas: latency/cost tradeoffs, deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), and integration patterns. quick question on timeline - are you looking at a pilot soon?
[00:01:03] Carlos: We're aiming for a pilot in 4-6 weeks, internal sign-off dependent on security review.
[00:01:08] Priya: Perfect. on integration: Redwood has first-class SDKs (Node, Python, Go) and a straight REST option. we also maintain LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors - we can share example repos. For embeddings and chat flows we recommend using our SDK which handles retries, streaming, and token accounting.
[00:01:26] Meera: if we use our gateway/proxy, do we need to open inbound from Redwood? or does traffic go outbound from our side?
[00:01:33] Avery: traffic is outbound from your side to Redwood's API for hosted. for dedicated/private we can operate within your VPC - with Private you get a customer-controlled control plane and optionally an on-prem package. so for PCI you'd likely consider Dedicated with VPC peering or Private depending on trust boundary.
[00:01:50] Sana: For KMS, can we bring our keys?
[00:01:53] Priya: yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated (via customer-managed keys). hosted supports encryption-at-rest but bring-your-own-key is available on enterprise plans.
[00:02:04] Liam: LangChain - any gotchas? we use LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for retrieval.
[00:02:10] Priya: our LangChain connector implements streaming and handles tokenization differences. LlamaIndex users usually point the vector store at our embeddings endpoint. watch for batching config - LlamaIndex can produce small frequent calls; we suggest a batching layer to combine small embedding requests into larger batches to improve cost.
[00:02:24] Meera: what about rate limits and quotas? we have spikes during settlement windows.
[00:02:29] Jordan: we have per-account and per-route quotas. for Hosted API we enforce burst limits but can increase burst windows for paid tiers. Dedicated gives you reserved throughput. We provide a quota config and token/hour limits, plus circuit-breakers.
[00:02:41] Carlos: So Dedicated sounds like reserved capacity - does that guarantee latency SLOs?
[00:02:45] Avery: Dedicated comes with predictable throughput & configurable autoscaling; SLA-backed uptime and latency targets are offered on enterprise contracts. we can show historic p50/p95 numbers for similar customers.
[00:02:56] Sana: audit logs - can we get per-request logging with redaction?
[00:03:00] Priya: yes we expose structured logs and tracing hooks; you can ingest into your observability stack (Datadog, Splunk). we also have token-level cost breakdowns in the console. redaction and PII filtering are supported in Private/Dedicated with customer-side transforms.
[00:03:14] Liam: SDK examples - do you have sample code where our gateway proxies requests to Redwood but preserves client IPs for rate-limiting?
[00:03:21] Jordan: we'll share patterns. typically you proxy through your gateway and add a header like x-forwarded-for; our routing can honor that with correct config. we also have API keys with strict scopes, and per-key quotas.
[00:03:33] Carlos: network - will Dedicated require us to run SG (security groups) and peer the VPC?
[00:03:38] Avery: Yes VPC peering or private link options. for Private on-prem, we do an installable control plane. For PCI workloads many customers pick Dedicated with VPC peering so infrastructure stays in their network boundary.
[00:03:50] Meera: ok good. can we run local mocks or a gateway that returns cached responses for common prompts? caching options?
[00:03:56] Priya: we support prefix and KV caching; you can run a local cache at your gateway. Redwood also supports automatic prefix caching and workload-aware batching that reduces per-token cost while keeping latency SLOs.
[00:04:10] Liam: regarding model variants and fallbacks - curious how Redwood handles graceful degradation if a region is saturated.
[00:04:16] Jordan: Smart routing - requests can route by policy (latency, cost, region) and fallback to compatible model variants or cross-region endpoints. that keeps app online during capacity constraints.
[00:04:27] Carlos: Competitors - we're also evaluating OpenAI and Bedrock. any notes on migration effort?
[00:04:33] Priya: API surface is similar, but you'll want to test prompt behavior and latencies; our SDKs try to minimize porting effort and we provide eval tooling to compare outputs and cost.
[00:04:44] Meera: can you run a benchmark against our sample prompts? we can provide expected QPS and a sample dataset.
[00:04:49] Avery: yes, we'll run a benchmark on Dedicated and Hosted variants. we'll need the prompt set, sequence length distribution, and QPS targets. we'll include token-level cost estimates.
[00:04:59] Liam: For LangChain and LlamaIndex flows we sometimes need streaming partial responses to the UI, is that supported?
[00:05:05] Priya: streaming is supported across SDKs and our LangChain connector. we also support function/tool calling patterns.
[00:05:11] Sana: any SOC2/ISO attestation docs we can review?
[00:05:14] Jordan: yes we have a security pack - SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, SOC2 report, data residency - we'll share the security whitepaper and the SOC2 artifacts under NDA.
[00:05:25] Carlos: cost question - with dedicated we pay a reserved capacity commit. how do we measure unit economics vs hosted?
[00:05:31] Avery: we provide per-token billing plus Dedicated has reserved monthly commits; our Optimize tooling suggests batching and quantization to reduce unit cost. we'll model a 6-mo TCO for comparison.
[00:05:43] Meera: what about model quantization and compatibility with our workloads?
[00:05:47] Priya: runtime supports quantization-friendly execution paths. we'll recommend quant profiles per model and per workload as part of the POC.
[00:05:56] Liam: any special headers or telemetry hooks to emit from our app so Redwood can surface per-route dashboards?
[00:06:00] Jordan: yes, send route metadata headers; our tracing hooks can correlate token cost to traces. we can provide dashboard templates for per-route latency and cost.
[00:06:08] Carlos: timeline recap - pilot in 4-6 weeks assuming security clears. bench in next week or two.
[00:06:14] Jordan: sounds right. we'll send initial artifacts and schedule the technical deep dive for benchmarks.
[00:06:19] Priya: quick note - for LlamaIndex folks, batching and embedding pooling is key; we can share a small adapter snippet that reduces calls by 60-80% for small documents.
[00:06:29] Meera: is there a proxy pattern you recommend for token accounting at the gateway? we need to reconcile cost per tenant.
[00:06:34] Priya: many customers do a per-tenant api-key mapping at the gateway and forward an internal tenant-id header; Redwood's billing and cost breakdowns map tokens to keys so you can attribute cost.
[00:06:45] Liam: ok great. any hurdles we should expect when using our existing internal proxy?
[00:06:50] Avery: proxy mostly fine; watch for connection pooling and keepalive to avoid cold starts. also ensure your gateway can handle streaming websockets if you need continuous partial tokens.
[00:07:02] Carlos: any other security items - data retention default?
[00:07:06] Jordan: default hosted logs shorter retention; enterprise plans allow configurable retention and deletion policies. Private gives you full control.
[00:07:14] Sana: good. could we get a sample SAML + SCIM setup doc?
[00:07:19] Jordan: yes we'll attach SAML/SSO/SCIM doc.
[00:07:23] Meera: A couple of minor things - do you support both REST and grpc?
[00:07:27] Priya: currently REST and streaming websocket; grpc is on the roadmap but not GA.
[00:07:33] Liam: for the benchmark, can we also see p50/p95 numbers for embeddings?
[00:07:37] Avery: yes we'll include embeddings latency/histograms per model.
[00:07:42] Carlos: ok let's move to next steps and close.
[00:07:45] Jordan: recap of next steps - we'll send pricing and Dedicated sizing, Priya will send SDK samples and LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, Avery will schedule the bench and run tests against your sample prompt set. Nimbus will provide QPS profile and security questions. We'll target the technical deep dive week of April 6th.
[00:08:03] Liam: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[00:08:06] Sana: thanks.
[00:08:08] Carlos: thanks all.
